title: 5 months, one director, AI for the code and the art: my roguelite deckbuilder has a free Steam demo. Here is what worked and what did not.
author: higashin900407
selftext:
Ink & Lore is a roguelite deckbuilder set inside a picture book that its author stopped drawing. Cards are one-use, you take two characters down as a pair, and the art falls apart the deeper you go.

I have been working on it for about five months. I am the director: I decide what the game is, I think up the staging and the moments that keep it interesting, I play every build, and I send back what feels wrong. The making itself is almost all AI.

What AI did

* Code: Claude Code. TypeScript and Phaser 3. About 6,300 automated tests.
* Art: every image, around 1,400 files, generated through Codex CLI with ChatGPT image generation.
* Writing: roughly 60% AI. I rewrote the other 40% by hand.
* Card text and numbers: AI drafts, I fix what bothers me.
* Translation (English, Chinese, Korean): all AI.

What worked

1. Design documents first. Every system has a written spec that the AI reads before touching code. When I change my mind, the document changes first.
2. Checks that cannot be skipped. A hook blocks the AI from finishing until lint, types and tests pass. This removed most of the "it says done but it is broken" moments.
3. Building immersion. I gave the enemies personalities: they have habits, they talk, and they panic when you break their habit. I also added motion comics at key moments of the story. Together these made the game feel like reading a picture book, which is what I wanted from the start.

What did not work

1. AI is bad at knowing what is fun. It can tell me a card is balanced. It cannot tell me the card is boring. That part is still me playing the game.
2. Leaving everything to the AI. A game needs things that keep it from getting boring. When I let the AI decide everything, I got a flat game that played the same way from start to finish. So I thought through each piece of staging myself, one by one.

The demo is free and has the whole first dungeon plus most of the second. Windows and Mac.

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4819010/Ink\_\_Lore/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4819010/Ink__Lore/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

Happy to go into detail on any part of the workflow.

comments.author: JasonKoh2
comments.body: Nice work! Can you explain more on how you use Codex CLI to create consistent art assets?

replies.author: higashin900407
replies.body:
Thanks! Four things did most of the work.

1. Reference images first. I make a character sheet before any scene, and attach it to every prompt. If a character looks different in a later scene, that look gets its own sheet.

2. One shared style block. The same style text is pasted at the top of every prompt, and I pass an existing finished image as a style reference.

Anything that fails the checks gets regenerated. I still look at every image myself at the end.

replies.author: JasonKoh2
replies.body: Thank you for sharing! Wish you all the best in the release!

comments.author: Wonderful_Craft_2332
comments.body: why would someone play this over slay the spire?

replies.author: higashin900407
replies.body:
Fair question. If you want the tightest deckbuilder, Slay the Spire is still the one to play.



Ink & Lore plays differently in a few ways:

\- Cards are one-use. There is no deck to cycle, so every card is a resource you spend, closer to items in a classic roguelike like Shiren the Wanderer.

\- You fight as a pair of two characters, with levels and equipment (sword, shield, bookmark).

\- Enemies have habits. If you break the habit, they panic and you get an opening.

\- The story is told like a picture book, with motion comics at key moments.



The demo is free, so it is easy to see if it is for you.

comments.author: IUsedToMakeMaps
comments.body:
Looks nice, video makes no sense, especially the first part. Why are you talking about features that are in every single deck-builder ever created? It seems like AI auto-created the subtitles. 

What is interesting about your system in particular? Or is it a clone with a good story?

replies.author: higashin900407
replies.body:
Thanks, and fair point on the video. The opening spends its time on things every deckbuilder has, and that is a mistake in the edit. The English captions are AI translated, like the rest of the game's English. I will recut it to lead with what is different.



What is different in the system:

\- Cards are one-use. You never cycle a deck. Every card is spent for good, so the question each turn is what to save, not what to draw.

\- When cards run low you fall back on basic attacks, levels and equipment, so a run feels closer to a classic roguelike like Shiren the Wanderer than to Slay the Spire.

\- You fight as a pair, and each character has a passive that feeds cards into your hand in its own way.

\- Enemies have habits. Break the habit and they panic, which gives you an opening.



So not a clone, but the story and the picture book staging are a big part of it too.
